reasons: The finding is claimed compliant with no redline and no comment, which matches the rendered output (paragraphs are unchanged) and the expected posture for a compliant classification.

The cited paragraphs contain no audit, inspection or verification right exercisable by Kubient against the Customer; p0001 is service-delivery cooperation, p0023 is payment (flowing from Vendor to Customer), and p0025 is a use restriction — none create audit exposure.

Because AUDIT constrains a Vendor right that burdens our party, the absence of any such right is at least as favourable as the preferred position; there is no walk-away language (no unlimited/unannounced audit, no Vendor remote access), so no redline is warranted and adding audit machinery would create a right that does not exist.
The failed deterministic check ('audit frequency limited') is expected here — no audit clause exists to bear frequency limits — and does not undercut the substance of the finding.
Rationale appropriately notes the forward-looking risk that future Exhibits could introduce Customer-side reporting requiring these limits, without over-flagging today.
